title: Prototype: Kaniko + Cosign Attestation with Argo gating for private deployments
content:
Status: prototype / working notes - not polished

Summary
--------
This doc captures a prototype flow for building and delivering signed container images for Redwood Private deployments (VPC/on-prem) using Kaniko (build), Cosign (signing/attestations), and ArgoCD/Argo Rollouts for gated progressive upgrades. Goal is to have a pragmatic pattern teams can adopt with Terraform modules that enforce image provenance and an automated rollback matrix for failures.

Why this exists
----------------
We keep seeing drift in how on-prem customers want guarantees about artifact provenance and safe upgrades. Existing playbooks in the drive focus on image-signing and gitops rotation (good), but we need a concrete CI->artifact->deploy prototype that:
- integrates build signing at CI level (non-root builders),
- produces attestations consumable by admission controllers in customer clusters,
- wires Argo gating (App-of-Apps + Rollouts) to reject/rollback on signal, and
- maps to Terraform modules for network/bastion/credentials so it is repeatable.

Scope / non-goals
------------------
In scope: CI pipelines, Kaniko config, Cosign usage patterns, README-style Terraform module notes for private deploys, Argo App patterns, and a rollback decision matrix.
Out of scope: complete airgap packaging (we will reference airgap docs), hardened KMS/HSM integration (callouts only), SLA contracts.

Assumptions
-----------
- Customer cluster runs ArgoCD and supports admission webhooks (OPA/Gatekeeper or a Cosign verifier Webhook).
- Private control plane (customer-managed networking) allows egress to Sigstore or we fallback to a local Rekor mirror.
- CI runners (self-hosted) have access to build context and a short-lived credential to push to customer registry (or a shared-managed registry in some deals).
- Teams prefer cosign (Sigstore) workflows for signing and OCI artifact attestations over bespoke solutions.

Architecture overview (high level)
----------------------------------
CI (GitHub Actions / self-hosted) -> Kaniko build -> push to registry (tag: semver+sha) -> cosign sign + attestation (in-toto/rekord) -> push attestation to registry and Rekor (or local rekor) -> GitOps: update image tag in repo -> ArgoCD detects change -> Argo Rollouts stepwise canary with probes -> Admission webhook verifies attestation before allowing new pods -> monitoring and rollback if SLO/regression signals breach.

CI pipeline notes (prototype)
----------------------------
- Build stage: Kaniko in a privileged build environment is avoided; use Kaniko executor with file system cache disabled when necessary. Example flags: --context=${{ github.workspace }} --dockerfile=Dockerfile --destination=${{ REGISTRY }}/${{ IMAGE }}:${{ VERSION }} --oci-layout-path=/kaniko/oci.
- Sign stage: cosign sign --key k8s://projects/_/locations/_/keyRings/_/cryptoKeys/_ ${REGISTRY}/${IMAGE}:${VERSION} and cosign attest --predicate=provenance.json. We prefer using k8s KMS-backed signing (k8s://) for private deployments where possible.
- Attestation format: using in-toto provenance predicate to capture build environment fingerprint (runner id, kaniko version, build args). Store the SBOM as a separate artifact (Syft or CycloneDX) and reference it in the attestation.
- CI runner security: require ephemeral signing keys, rotate per-run via short-lived KMS keys or workload identity (where supported).

Terraform module notes (for private deploys)
--------------------------------------------
Objective: Provide a small set of modules customers can copy/consume to provision the infra required for the gated deploy flow: VPC, egress NAT, bastion/proxy for registry access, and argocd bootstrap.
- Module: private-deploy-networking: outputs vpc id, subnet ids, nat config (for controlled egress).
- Module: private-deploy-bastion: simple bastion autoscaling group + ssh-proxy config for CI runners needing registry push access.
- Module: argocd-install: installs ArgoCD with helm chart values to enable admin token rotation and TLS. Exposes argocd API via private LB.
- Module: admission-verifier: installs a small Helm chart that wires Cosign/rego policy with a configurable Rekor endpoint.
Notes: keep modules small and composable. Provide example var files for onprem vs VPC-mode. Document a 'bring-your-own-rekor' option vs 'managed rekor mirror'.

Helm / release mechanics and Argo patterns
-----------------------------------------
- App-of-Apps: root repo stores customer app repo references. Root Argo App triggers downstream apps. Keep image tag updates in the downstream app repo (this allows PR review before a change flows to Argo).
- Image update flow: we propose a GitHub Action that opens a PR in the app repo when a new signed image is available. That PR must pass acceptance tests, then be merged to trigger Argo.
- Argo Rollouts: prefer linear/canary with analysis: 10% -> 30% -> 100%, with automated abort on failed analysis. Analysis can include: readiness probe errors, error budget burn, latency regressions (via Prom or Grafana alerts).
- Helm charts: charts must use image.tag and image.digest as acceptable values. Recommended pattern: set image.digest from the attestation (stronger) but allow tag for human inspection. Use Helmfile or values templating to inject digests if available.

Admission validation and attestation verification
--------------------------------------------------
- Option A (recommended): Cosign admission webhook running in cluster verifies signature and optional SBOM attestation. Reject pods whose image lacks a valid attestation in Rekor or whose predicate does not meet the team policy.
- Option B: OPA/Gatekeeper policy queries a local cache/repository of attestations and rejects based on custom rules.
- Fallback for airgapped: use a local Rekor + signed mirror of cosign public keys stored in KMS. Document how to bootstrap Rekor and rotate the trusted root.

Rollback matrix (prototype)
---------------------------
We need a clear decision matrix that maps signals to actions. Example: 
- Fatal: API server crash loops (>50% nodes) -> immediate full rollback to last-known-good release.
- Severe: 5xx spike > 3x baseline sustained 10 minutes -> automated rollback to previous image digest, and open incident.
- Degradation: latency P95 increase 2x for 5 minutes -> pause rollout, promote canary to limited traffic (manual review) or rollback depending on owner decision.
- Policy failure: admission webhook rejects pods -> block rollouts, mark PR as failed, do not rollback automatically (no new pods deployed).
Implementation: Argo Rollouts with analysis and webhooks. Keep a small operator script that can trigger rollbacks by patching Argo Rollout's rolloutPlan to force rollback to the recorded stable revision.

Preflight checklist (per-release)
---------------------------------
- [ ] Build artifact exists with cosign signature and Rekor entry (reproducible check).
- [ ] SBOM uploaded and references match the attestation predicate.
- [ ] Helm values PR created and passes unit tests (linting, helm template).
- [ ] Acceptance tests pass against staging cluster with admission webhook enabled.
- [ ] Argo Rollouts config for strategy + analysis configured.
- [ ] Terraform plan for any infra changes reviewed.

Testing plan
------------
- Unit: helm lint, k8s manifest validation, cosign verification test using test key pair.
- Integration: end-to-end in staging: build/sign/push -> PR update -> Argo applies -> canary -> run synthetic traffic, chaos tests (simulated node failure), and policy rejection tests.
- Airgap test: mirror registry into airgapped env, seed Rekor mirror, test deployment with verification switching to local Rekor.

Operational playbook (incident steps)
------------------------------------
1. Identify failing rollout via alerts/Argo events.
2. Check attestation state (rekor search) for image digest.
3. If policy violation -> check key rotation logs and reconfigure webhook trust.
4. If performance/functional failure -> trigger Argo Rollout rollback, notify on-call, create incident ticket.
5. If rollback fails -> escalate to SRE, consider scaling replica count or short-term traffic shifting to a compatible region/pool.

Example commands (notes)
------------------------
- cosign verify --key k8s://projects/... ${REGISTRY}/${IMAGE}:${TAG} 
- rekor-cli search --artifact ${DIGEST} --format json
- kubectl argo rollouts get rollout <name> --watch
- kaniko: executor:latest --context ... --destination ...

Open questions / TODOs
----------------------
- Key management: do we recommend k8s:// KMS for all customers? Document tradeoffs for HSM vs managed KMS.
- Rekor availability: for customers who cannot reach public Rekor, we need a secure bake-and-ship process for Rekor snapshots. Outline this in separate airgap playbook.
- How do we best surface predicate metadata in PRs for reviewers (SBOM summary, base image lineage)?
- Who owns the on-call runbook for admission webhook failures in customer-managed clusters? (SRE vs customer)

Next steps (practical)
----------------------
- Finish a small prototype repo: github.com/redwood-inference/private-deploy-attest-proto with: GH Action workflow, Kaniko example, Cosign sign/attest steps, sample Helm chart and small Argo app-of-apps. (ACTION: Evan to bootstrap: INFRA-842)
- Draft a short runbook for airgapped Rekor mirroring and key bootstrap (María).
- Create Terraform example var files for AWS VPC vs on-prem network emulation (Liam).
- Schedule a 90-minute sync with SRE and Solutions Eng to review rollback matrix and support boundaries.

References and helpful links
----------------------------
- Sigstore / Cosign: https://sigstore.dev
- Rekor: https://github.com/sigstore/rekor
- Notary v2 notes: https://github.com/notaryproject/notary
- Syft (SBOM): https://github.com/anchore/syft
- Argo Rollouts analysis docs: https://argoproj.github.io/argo-rollouts/

Notes to self
-------------
- Keep the prototype small and opinionated; teams can opt into specific pieces (e.g., signing only, or signing + webhook).
- Document short path to onboard customers that already run ArgoCD vs customers that do not.
